subject: High RAM usage by applying which.min() on >50,000 rows

messages.author: 9485431b4435a3a9
messages.subject: High RAM usage by applying which.min() on >50,000 rows
parts:
Hello,

I have a table of >50,000 rows of exon array data, and I need find the first exon for each gene based on the start and end columns. 

So, for genes on the positive strand, I need the rows that have the minimum value for "start" for each group of exons with a common "gene".

I've tried:
pos_first = ddply(pos_strand, .(gene), function(x)x[which.min(x$start),] )

However, this quickly balloons to >6 GB of RAM usage, which leaves no free RAM, and gets very slow. This seems kind of odd to me, since the whole data frame as a TSV is ~17 MB. Does plyr split the data frame up and then apply a function to each piece, or am I ending up with as many copies of the whole table as there are genes?

If I'm not applying ddply correctly, or if there's a better way to get at this, please let me know!

Thanks!
-Lucas

messages.author: 7e921b60a6dff156
messages.subject: Re: High RAM usage by applying which.min() on >50,000 rows
parts:
Ugh, major typos:

> R> install.packages("data.table")
> R> library(data.table)
> R> pot_strand <- as.data.table(pos_strand)
> R> setkeyv(pos_strand, "gene")
> R> pos_first <- post_strand[, .SD[which.min(start)], by="gene"]

Should be:

R> pos_strand <- as.data.table(pos_strand)
R> setkeyv(pos_strand, "gene")
R> pos_first <- pos_strand[, .SD[which.min(start)], by="gene"]

... hopefully I didn't mess it up again, but hopefully you get the idea.

-steve

Thanks, Steve! 

That works very well, and I've learned a bit about data.table, too.

I got another reply by email that recommended I take a look at data.table - I'm not sure why it's not showing up here - but I couldn't figure out how to get it to return the whole row, which your example does very well (with .SD[] ?).

I'm still curious why ddply seems to struggle in this instance, but I can get on with my analysis using data.table.

-Lucas
